levels.name: Functional
levels.summary: Code runs and basic tooling exists, but setup is manual and validation is thin.

levels.name: Documented
levels.summary: Workflows are written down for humans and agents; local guardrails catch mistakes early.

levels.name: Standardized
levels.summary: Processes are enforced by automation: integration tests, security scanning, observability.

levels.name: Optimized
levels.summary: Feedback loops are fast and measured; quality and delivery are tracked continuously.

levels.name: Autonomous
levels.summary: The system checks and improves itself; agents can take on long-running work end to end.

pillars.name: Style & Validation
pillars.why: Linters, type checkers and formatters catch mistakes in seconds, so agents don't burn cycles waiting on CI to find a typo.

pillars.name: Build System
pillars.why: Deterministic, documented build and release commands let an agent verify its change compiles and ships without guessing flags.

pillars.name: Testing
pillars.why: Fast, locally runnable tests are the agent's feedback loop: change, run, read the failure, iterate.

pillars.name: Documentation
pillars.why: Written instructions replace tribal knowledge. Agents only know what is discoverable in the repo.

pillars.name: Dev Environment
pillars.why: Reproducible environments remove 'works on my machine' for humans and agents alike.

pillars.name: Debugging & Observability
pillars.why: Logs, traces and metrics turn 'it failed' into 'it failed because X was null in Y', which an agent can act on.

pillars.name: Security & Governance
pillars.why: Agents move fast. Branch protection, secret scanning and ownership rules make sure they move fast safely.

pillars.name: Task Discovery
pillars.why: Structured issues, labels and templates let an agent find, scope and report on work without a human translating.

pillars.name: Product & Experimentation
pillars.why: Analytics and experiments let an agent see whether a change mattered, not just whether it compiled.

lanes.name: Auto-fix
lanes.summary: Small, reversible changes decided by facts already in the repo. The agent can apply these directly.

lanes.name: Your call
lanes.summary: A choice of tool, policy or architecture. The agent lays out options and trade-offs; you decide.

lanes.name: Manual
lanes.summary: Outside the repo: platform settings or team process. The agent gives exact steps; you do it.

criteria.name: Linter configured
criteria.pass: A linter is configured for the app's primary language (ESLint, Biome, Ruff, Flake8, Pylint, golangci-lint, Clippy, RuboCop, Checkstyle, SwiftLint, ktlint, etc.).
criteria.fix: Add the ecosystem-default linter with a committed config and a `lint` script/target.

criteria.name: Type checking
criteria.pass: The language is statically typed (Go, Rust, Java, C#, Kotlin, Swift, C/C++), or a type checker is configured (tsconfig.json, mypy, pyright, Sorbet, etc.).
criteria.fix: Add TypeScript/tsconfig or mypy/pyright with a `typecheck` command.

criteria.name: Code formatter
criteria.pass: An automatic formatter is configured or built into the toolchain and used (Prettier, Biome, Black, Ruff format, gofmt, rustfmt, clang-format, etc.).
criteria.fix: Add the ecosystem formatter with a config file and a `format` command.

criteria.name: Strict typing
criteria.pass: Type checking runs in strict mode (`strict: true` in tsconfig, mypy `strict = true`, pyright `strict`), or the language is statically typed by default.
criteria.fix: Turn on strict mode; fix or explicitly suppress the resulting errors.

criteria.name: Pre-commit hooks
criteria.pass: Local hooks run lint/format/type checks before commit (pre-commit, Husky, lefthook, simple-git-hooks, lint-staged, a committed .githooks/ wired via core.hooksPath).
criteria.fix: Add pre-commit/Husky/lefthook running the fast checks on staged files.

criteria.name: Checks run as the agent edits
criteria.pass: Agent hooks run fast checks automatically after edits or before finishing (Claude Code/Droid hooks in settings, .cursor/hooks.json, Copilot or Cline hooks), so formatting and type errors are caught without relying on instructions.
criteria.fix: Add a post-edit hook that runs the formatter and a stop hook that runs lint + typecheck.

criteria.name: Naming conventions
criteria.pass: Naming conventions are documented (AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING, style guide) or enforced by lint rules (e.g. ESLint naming-convention, pep8-naming).
criteria.fix: Document conventions in AGENTS.md and/or enable a naming lint rule.

criteria.name: Large file guard
criteria.pass: Something prevents large/binary files from landing in git: Git LFS via .gitattributes, a check-added-large-files hook, or a CI size check.
criteria.fix: Add `check-added-large-files` to pre-commit or a CI size check; use LFS for binaries.

criteria.name: Tech debt tracking
criteria.pass: TODO/FIXME comments are tracked or constrained: a lint rule requiring ticket references, a TODO scanner in CI, or a debt register that is maintained.
criteria.fix: Require `TODO(#123)` format via lint rule, or add a TODO scanner to CI.

criteria.name: Dead code detection
criteria.pass: A dedicated detector for unused exports, files or functions runs in CI or hooks (knip, ts-prune, vulture, deadcode, unparam). General unused-import/unused-variable lint rules don't count on their own.
criteria.fix: Add knip/vulture/deadcode to CI.

criteria.name: Duplicate code detection
criteria.pass: Copy-paste detection runs in CI (jscpd, PMD CPD, SonarQube duplication gate, etc.).
criteria.fix: Add jscpd (or the ecosystem equivalent) with a threshold in CI.

criteria.name: Complexity limits
criteria.pass: Function complexity is measured and limited (ESLint `complexity`, Ruff C901/mccabe, gocyclo, Clippy cognitive_complexity, Sonar, etc.).
criteria.fix: Enable a complexity rule with a sensible max in the existing linter.

criteria.name: Module boundaries enforced
criteria.pass: Architectural boundaries are enforced by tooling (dependency-cruiser, eslint-plugin-boundaries, Nx module boundaries, import-linter, ArchUnit, Go internal/ packages used deliberately), ideally with error messages that say how to fix the violation.
criteria.fix: Add dependency-cruiser/import-linter rules for the main layers.

criteria.name: N+1 query detection
criteria.pass: Apps that use an ORM/database have N+1 detection (Bullet, nplusone, Django assertNumQueries patterns, Prisma/Hibernate query logging checks). Skip if the app has no database access.
criteria.fix: Add an N+1 detector in test mode.

criteria.name: Build command documented
criteria.pass: The exact commands to install, build and run are written down (README, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING) or exposed as obvious scripts (package.json scripts, Makefile, justfile, Taskfile).
criteria.fix: Add a 'Commands' section to AGENTS.md listing install/build/test/lint/run.

criteria.name: Dependencies locked
criteria.pass: A lockfile is committed (package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, bun.lock(b), uv.lock, poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock, Cargo.lock for binaries, go.sum, Gemfile.lock, composer.lock, etc.).
criteria.fix: Generate and commit the lockfile; stop ignoring it.

criteria.name: VCS CLI available
criteria.pass: The hosting platform's CLI (gh, glab, az repos, etc.) is installed and authenticated in the environment the agent runs in, so it can open PRs and read CI/issue state.
criteria.fix: Install and authenticate `gh`/`glab` in the dev environment or devcontainer.

criteria.name: Single-command setup
criteria.pass: A fresh clone can be bootstrapped with one documented command (`make setup`, `./scripts/bootstrap`, `just setup`, `npm run setup`, devcontainer, `mise install && ...`).
criteria.fix: Add a bootstrap script/target that installs deps, copies env templates and prepares local services.

criteria.name: Agents already in the loop
criteria.pass: There is evidence agents already work here: agent co-author trailers in recent commits, agent config dirs (.claude/, .cursor/, .codex/, .factory/, .github/copilot-instructions.md), or agent bot PRs.
criteria.fix: Start routing small tasks through an agent; commit its config so the setup is shared.

criteria.name: Automated PR review
criteria.pass: Pull requests get automated review beyond CI pass/fail: an AI reviewer, a review bot, Danger, or policy bots that comment on PRs.
criteria.fix: Enable an AI code reviewer or Danger rules on PRs.

criteria.name: Release automation
criteria.pass: Releases/deploys are triggered by automation (CD workflow on merge/tag, semantic-release, changesets, release-please, GoReleaser, platform auto-deploy like Vercel/Netlify/Fly connected to the repo).
criteria.fix: Add a CD workflow on merge to main or a tag-driven release tool.

criteria.name: Monorepo tooling
criteria.pass: Multi-app repos use workspace tooling (pnpm/npm/yarn workspaces, Turborepo, Nx, Bazel, Pants, Cargo/Go workspaces, uv workspaces). Skip for single-app repos.
criteria.fix: Declare workspaces and add a task runner (Turborepo/Nx) for cross-app commands.

criteria.name: Unused dependency detection
criteria.pass: Unused dependencies are detected in CI or hooks (knip, depcheck, deptry, cargo-udeps/machete, `go mod tidy` diff check).
criteria.fix: Add knip/depcheck/deptry/`go mod tidy -diff` to CI.

criteria.name: Fast CI feedback
criteria.pass: The slowest workflow that runs on pull requests typically finishes in about 10 minutes or less (median of recent runs). Fail if there is no CI at all.
criteria.fix: Cache dependencies, split/parallelize jobs, run only affected targets.

criteria.name: Regular deployments
criteria.pass: Releases or deploys happen regularly (e.g. several in the last 90 days, visible via tags, releases, or deploy workflow runs). Skip for libraries with no deploy target only if releases also aren't applicable.
criteria.fix: Automate releases so shipping is cheap; release smaller and more often.

criteria.name: Build performance tracked
criteria.pass: Builds are cached or measured: dependency or build caching in CI (actions/cache, setup-* cache), Turborepo/Nx/Bazel remote cache, sccache, or CI timing dashboards and build-time budgets.
criteria.fix: Enable a build cache and track build durations in CI.

criteria.name: Release notes automated
criteria.pass: Changelogs or release notes are generated from commits/PRs (changesets, release-please, semantic-release, git-cliff, GitHub generated notes, conventional commits enforced).
criteria.fix: Adopt conventional commits + release-please/changesets.

criteria.name: Feature flags
criteria.pass: Deployed apps have a feature flag system (LaunchDarkly, Unleash, GrowthBook, Flagsmith, PostHog flags, Statsig, OpenFeature, or a deliberate in-house system). Skip for libraries/CLIs.
criteria.fix: Introduce a flag provider (OpenFeature-compatible) so risky changes can ship dark.

criteria.name: Bundle size guard
criteria.pass: Frontend/bundled apps have a size budget or analyzer in CI (size-limit, bundlesize, bundle analyzer with thresholds, Lighthouse CI budgets). Skip for non-bundled apps.
criteria.fix: Add size-limit or a bundle budget check to CI.

criteria.name: Version drift detection
criteria.pass: Monorepos keep shared dependency versions aligned (syncpack, manypkg, pnpm catalogs, Renovate group rules, Bazel/Gradle version catalogs). Skip for single-app repos.
criteria.fix: Add syncpack/manypkg or pnpm catalogs.

criteria.name: Progressive rollout
criteria.pass: Deploys can roll out gradually (canary, percentage rollouts, blue/green, Argo Rollouts, Flagger, platform traffic splitting). Skip for libraries/CLIs.
criteria.fix: Add canary or percentage rollout to the deploy path.

criteria.name: Automated rollback
criteria.pass: There is a documented one-step or automatic rollback (platform instant rollback, rollback workflow, Argo/Flagger auto-abort on bad metrics). Skip for libraries/CLIs.
criteria.fix: Document the rollback command; add automatic abort on failed health checks.

criteria.name: Stale flag cleanup
criteria.pass: Stale feature flags are detected and cleaned up (flag provider stale reports wired to issues, Piranha, a CI check). Skip if there is no flag system.
criteria.fix: Wire stale-flag reports into issues or add a cleanup check.

criteria.name: Unit tests exist
criteria.pass: The app has meaningful unit tests (test files alongside or in a tests/ dir; more than a placeholder).
criteria.fix: Add a test framework and a first set of tests around core logic.

criteria.name: Tests runnable locally
criteria.pass: There is a documented, single command that runs the tests locally without special credentials and exits on its own (no watch mode or prompts): `npm test`, `pytest`, `go test ./...`, `cargo test`, `make test`.
criteria.fix: Expose one `test` command and document it in AGENTS.md.

criteria.name: Single-test command documented
criteria.pass: Docs show how to run one test file or case (e.g. `pytest path::test_x`, `vitest run file`, `go test -run Name`, `cargo test name`), so agents can iterate without running the whole suite.
criteria.fix: Add a one-line 'run a single test' example to AGENTS.md.

criteria.name: Test naming conventions
criteria.pass: Test files follow a consistent, tool-recognized pattern (*.test.ts, *_test.go, test_*.py, configured testMatch/testpaths).
criteria.fix: Pick one pattern and configure the runner to match it.

criteria.name: Integration / E2E tests
criteria.pass: There are tests that exercise components together or end to end (integration/ or e2e/ suites, Playwright, Cypress, testcontainers, API tests against a running service).
criteria.fix: Add an integration or Playwright/E2E suite for the critical path.

criteria.name: Agent can see the running app
criteria.pass: Web apps give agents a way to check the real UI: Playwright/Cypress runnable locally and documented for agents, or a browser automation MCP server configured (.mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json). Skip for apps without a UI.
criteria.fix: Add a Playwright smoke test for the main flow and document the command, or configure a browser MCP server.

criteria.name: Test isolation
criteria.pass: Tests are isolated and parallel-safe: run in parallel (pytest-xdist, Jest/Vitest workers, go test -race/-parallel), use fixtures/factories, no shared mutable global state or order dependence.
criteria.fix: Enable parallel test runs and fix order-dependent tests.

criteria.name: Coverage tracked
criteria.pass: Coverage is measured and either enforced with a threshold or reported on PRs (coverage thresholds in config, Codecov/Coveralls, CI coverage gate).
criteria.fix: Collect coverage in CI and set a floor that ratchets upward.

criteria.name: Flaky test detection
criteria.pass: Flaky tests are detected or quarantined (retry-and-report, quarantine lists, Trunk/BuildPulse/Datadog CI visibility, stress-run jobs, flaky-test issue automation).
criteria.fix: Turn on test retries with reporting, and quarantine known-flaky tests.

criteria.name: Test performance tracked
criteria.pass: Test durations or benchmarks are tracked (slowest-test reporting, --durations in CI, benchmark workflows, CI analytics).
criteria.fix: Report slowest tests in CI; add benchmarks for hot paths.

criteria.name: README
criteria.pass: A README exists and explains what the project is and how to get it running (not just a title or template boilerplate).
criteria.fix: Write a README with purpose, setup, and run/test commands.

criteria.name: Agent instructions file
criteria.pass: An agent instructions file exists with real, repo-specific content: AGENTS.md (read by nearly every harness) or a harness-specific equivalent (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursor/rules, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .clinerules). It must give commands and conventions, not just a stub or a generic overview.
criteria.fix: Write a short AGENTS.md: exact commands first, then conventions and gotchas only a teammate would know. Skip the directory tour; generated overviews measurably don't help agents.

criteria.name: Agent instructions stay lean and accurate
criteria.pass: The main agent instructions file is concise (about 200 lines or fewer), isn't an unedited generated dump, and every file path and script it references exists. Longer material lives in linked docs or scoped rules. Skip if there is no agent instructions file yet (agents_md fails).
criteria.fix: Cut the file to commands, conventions and gotchas; move reference material into docs/ and link to it; fix any stale paths.

criteria.name: Docs kept fresh
criteria.pass: Key docs in the repo (README, AGENTS.md or equivalent, CONTRIBUTING) were each updated within 180 days of the repository's latest commit, so they move with the code. A stub that only links elsewhere counts as present but not substantive.
criteria.fix: Review and refresh README/AGENTS.md against the current commands.

criteria.name: Agent skills / commands
criteria.pass: Reusable agent skills or commands for working on this repo are committed where harnesses discover them (.claude/skills, .agents/skills, .factory/skills, .codex/skills, .cursor/skills, .github/skills, or custom slash-command/prompt dirs). Skills shipped as package data for end users don't count.
criteria.fix: Capture a repeated workflow (release, migration, debugging) as a SKILL.md.

criteria.name: Scoped instructions
criteria.pass: Instructions load only where they're relevant: nested AGENTS.md in subprojects, path-scoped rules (.claude/rules with paths, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md with applyTo, .cursor/rules with globs), or skills. Skip for small codebases (under ~100 source files, not counting tests and docs).
criteria.fix: Move area-specific guidance out of the root file into nested AGENTS.md files or path-scoped rules.

criteria.name: API schema documented
criteria.pass: Apps that expose an API publish a machine-readable schema (OpenAPI/Swagger, GraphQL SDL, protobuf, tRPC/zod schemas exported, JSON Schema). Skip for apps with no API surface.
criteria.fix: Generate an OpenAPI spec (or SDL) from the code and commit/serve it.

criteria.name: Architecture documented
criteria.pass: Architecture or key flows are documented (ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/ with diagrams, Mermaid/PlantUML, ADRs) beyond what the README says.
criteria.fix: Add ARCHITECTURE.md with a component map and one or two key request flows.

criteria.name: Docs generated
criteria.pass: Some docs are generated from source and kept in sync automatically (TypeDoc, Sphinx autodoc, rustdoc/godoc published, OpenAPI generation in CI, docs site build).
criteria.fix: Generate API/reference docs in CI.

criteria.name: Agent instructions verified
criteria.pass: Something keeps agent instructions true: a CI job that runs the documented commands or checks referenced paths, an automated AGENTS.md updater, or a scheduled agent/job that gardens stale docs. Skip if there are no agent instructions yet.
criteria.fix: Add a CI job that executes the commands listed in AGENTS.md.

criteria.name: Env template
criteria.pass: Required environment variables are documented in a committed template (.env.example, .env.sample, .env.template) or a documented config section. Skip if the app needs no env configuration.
criteria.fix: Commit .env.example listing every variable with a safe placeholder and a comment.

criteria.name: Reproducible environment
criteria.pass: A reproducible, non-interactive dev environment is defined: .devcontainer/devcontainer.json, Nix flake/shell, devbox.json, a documented dev Dockerfile/compose setup, or an agent setup file such as .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml.
criteria.fix: Add .devcontainer/devcontainer.json with the toolchain and post-create setup.

criteria.name: Local services
criteria.pass: Backing services (DB, cache, queues) can be started locally with one command (docker-compose, Tilt, Skaffold, supabase start, testcontainers). Skip if there are no backing services.
criteria.fix: Add compose.yaml for the backing services and document `docker compose up`.

criteria.name: Schema as code
criteria.pass: Apps that use a database manage schema as code (migrations dir, Prisma/Drizzle schema, Alembic, Rails/Django migrations, Flyway, Atlas). Skip if there is no database.
criteria.fix: Adopt a migration tool and commit the schema.

criteria.name: Environment verified
criteria.pass: The reproducible environment is exercised in CI (devcontainers/ci action, Nix build in CI, compose-based test job) so it doesn't rot. Skip if no environment definition exists (devcontainer already fails).
criteria.fix: Build the devcontainer (or Nix shell) in CI.

criteria.name: Parallel-agent friendly
criteria.pass: Several agents can work at once without colliding: ports and database URLs come from env, test databases are ephemeral or per-run, and setup works in a fresh git worktree (.worktreeinclude or documented). Skip for libraries without services.
criteria.fix: Read PORT/DATABASE_URL from env, give tests their own database, and document worktree setup.

criteria.name: Structured logging
criteria.pass: Deployed services log through a structured logger (pino, winston JSON, structlog, zap, slog, tracing, logback JSON) instead of bare print/console.log. Skip for libraries.
criteria.fix: Adopt a structured logger with request/trace IDs in every line.

criteria.name: Logs an agent can read
criteria.pass: Local dev logs go somewhere an agent can read on demand (a log file, `make logs`, `docker compose logs`, a documented command) rather than only an interactive terminal. Skip for libraries and CLIs.
criteria.fix: Add a `logs` script or make target and mention it in AGENTS.md.

criteria.name: Tracing
criteria.pass: Services emit traces (OpenTelemetry, Datadog APM, Honeycomb, Sentry performance, X-Ray) with trace context propagated. Skip for libraries/CLIs.
criteria.fix: Add OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation and export to your backend.

criteria.name: Metrics
criteria.pass: Services expose or ship runtime metrics (Prometheus client, StatsD, OpenTelemetry metrics, Datadog, platform analytics). Skip for libraries/CLIs.
criteria.fix: Expose RED metrics (rate, errors, duration) via OpenTelemetry or Prometheus.

criteria.name: Error tracking
criteria.pass: Errors are captured with context (Sentry, Bugsnag, Rollbar, Honeybadger, Datadog error tracking) including release/user/request tags. Skip for libraries.
criteria.fix: Add Sentry (or equivalent) with release and environment tags.

criteria.name: Health checks
criteria.pass: Services expose health/readiness endpoints or probes (/health, /healthz, /ready, k8s probes, platform health checks). Skip for libraries/CLIs/static sites.
criteria.fix: Add /healthz (liveness) and /readyz (dependencies) endpoints.

criteria.name: Alerting
criteria.pass: Alert rules are defined as code or documented (Prometheus/Alertmanager rules, Datadog/Grafana monitors-as-code, PagerDuty/Opsgenie integration, Sentry alert rules referenced). Skip for libraries.
criteria.fix: Define alerts as code for error rate and latency SLOs.

criteria.name: Deploy observability
criteria.pass: Deploys are visible in monitoring (release markers in Sentry/Datadog, deploy annotations, dashboards linked from docs) so regressions can be tied to a release. Skip for libraries.
criteria.fix: Send release/deploy markers from the deploy workflow.

criteria.name: Profiling
criteria.pass: Performance can be profiled in a standard way (pprof endpoints, continuous profiling like Pyroscope/Datadog, documented profiling scripts, benchmark harnesses).
criteria.fix: Expose pprof/py-spy recipes or enable continuous profiling.

criteria.name: Runbooks
criteria.pass: Operational runbooks exist (runbooks/ or docs/ops, incident playbooks, linked from alerts or docs). Skip for libraries.
criteria.fix: Write runbooks for the top alerts and common incidents.

criteria.name: Code quality metrics
criteria.pass: Code health is measured over time (coverage trend, SonarQube/CodeClimate/Codacy, DeepSource, CI-published quality reports).
criteria.fix: Publish coverage and lint debt to a dashboard or PR comments.

criteria.name: Resilience patterns
criteria.pass: Calls to external dependencies use circuit breakers/bulkheads/timeouts via a library or mesh (opossum, resilience4j, Polly, pybreaker, gobreaker, Istio/Envoy policies). Skip for apps without external dependencies.
criteria.fix: Wrap outbound calls with timeouts + a circuit breaker library.

criteria.name: Comprehensive .gitignore
criteria.pass: .gitignore excludes secrets (.env, key files), dependency dirs, build output and editor/OS junk for the languages in use, and no such files are tracked.
criteria.fix: Extend .gitignore from the github/gitignore template for each language; untrack anything sensitive.

criteria.name: Branch protection
criteria.pass: The default branch is protected (branch protection or rulesets requiring PRs/reviews/status checks). Verify with the platform CLI/API when possible.
criteria.fix: Require PRs and passing checks on the default branch.

criteria.name: CODEOWNERS
criteria.pass: A CODEOWNERS file exists (root, .github/ or docs/) assigning owners to paths.
criteria.fix: Add .github/CODEOWNERS with at least a default owner.

criteria.name: Agent config is owned
criteria.pass: Changes to what agents are told are reviewed: CODEOWNERS covers AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .cursor/, .agents/, MCP configs and .github/copilot-* (a catch-all `*` owner counts). Skip if the repo has no agent instruction or config files.
criteria.fix: Add CODEOWNERS entries for agent instruction and config files.

criteria.name: Secret scanning
criteria.pass: Secrets are scanned for: platform secret scanning/push protection enabled, or gitleaks/trufflehog/detect-secrets in hooks or CI.
criteria.fix: Enable push protection, or add gitleaks to pre-commit and CI.

criteria.name: Dependency updates automated
criteria.pass: Dependency updates are automated (Dependabot config, Renovate config, or equivalent).
criteria.fix: Add .github/dependabot.yml or renovate.json.

criteria.name: Secrets management
criteria.pass: Runtime secrets come from a manager or platform store (env injected by platform, Vault, AWS/GCP/Azure secret managers, Doppler, 1Password, SOPS) and no secrets are hardcoded in source.
criteria.fix: Move secrets to the platform's secret store; read them from env at runtime.

criteria.name: Agent guardrails in config
criteria.pass: Rules agents must follow are enforced by committed config, not only prose: permission deny/allow lists or sandbox settings (.claude/settings.json, .codex/config.toml, .cursor/ or .factory/ settings, Copilot agent firewall config) that at least keep agents out of secrets like .env.
criteria.fix: Commit shared agent settings that deny reads of .env and secrets/ and allow the safe dev commands.

criteria.name: Log scrubbing
criteria.pass: Logs redact sensitive fields (logger redact config, scrubbing processors, Sentry beforeSend scrubbing). Skip for libraries and CLIs.
criteria.fix: Configure logger redaction paths for tokens, passwords and PII.

criteria.name: PII handling
criteria.pass: Apps that handle personal data have an explicit approach (data classification, PII-tagged fields, encryption at rest for sensitive columns, documented retention). Skip if no personal data.
criteria.fix: Document which fields are PII and how they're protected and retained.

criteria.name: Static security analysis
criteria.pass: Application source or dependencies are scanned for vulnerabilities on PRs (CodeQL, Semgrep, Snyk, SonarQube security, Bandit, gosec, npm/pip/cargo audit, osv-scanner). Linters that only scan CI workflow files (e.g. zizmor, actionlint) don't count.
criteria.fix: Enable CodeQL or add Semgrep to CI.

criteria.name: MCP config hygiene
criteria.pass: Committed MCP server configs keep secrets out (env references only), pin server versions instead of @latest, and don't combine untrusted input, private data and outbound access in one setup. Skip if no MCP config is committed.
criteria.fix: Replace inline tokens with env references, pin server versions, and drop servers nobody uses.

criteria.name: Dynamic security testing
criteria.pass: Running web apps are scanned dynamically (OWASP ZAP, Burp, Nuclei, StackHawk) in CI or on a schedule. Skip for non-web apps.
criteria.fix: Run a ZAP baseline scan against a preview deployment.

criteria.name: Privacy compliance
criteria.pass: User-facing products that collect personal data have privacy controls in code (consent management, data export/deletion paths, documented DPA/GDPR handling). Skip otherwise.
criteria.fix: Implement data export/deletion flows and consent handling.

criteria.name: Issue templates
criteria.pass: Issue templates or forms exist (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, .gitlab/issue_templates/) and ask for reproduction steps or acceptance criteria, so an agent can tell when the work is done.
criteria.fix: Add bug and feature templates that ask for repro steps and acceptance criteria.

criteria.name: PR template
criteria.pass: A pull/merge request template exists (pull_request_template.md in root, .github/ or docs/; .gitlab/merge_request_templates/).
criteria.fix: Add .github/pull_request_template.md with summary, testing and risk sections.

criteria.name: Issue labels
criteria.pass: Issues use a deliberate label taxonomy beyond the platform defaults (type, area, priority), visible via the platform CLI/API or a labels config file.
criteria.fix: Define type/area/priority labels (labels-as-code if possible).

criteria.name: Healthy backlog
criteria.pass: Open issues are descriptive and triaged: clear titles, bodies with context, labels applied, stale issues closed. Skip if the repo doesn't use an issue tracker visible to the agent.
criteria.fix: Triage the backlog; add a stale bot and require labels.

criteria.name: Plans live in the repo
